title: Should advanced settings appear upfront in project setup?
scope: Hypothetical illustrative decision, not a historical claim about any company
primary_job: Connect an existing application and run a working preview
primary_user: Application developer new to the product (experience with code may still be high)
uncertainties: Actual required configurations vary by repository
No measured frequency of advanced settings use
No user validation of proposed options

options.name: All settings upfront
options.description: Show all configuration controls in one dense flow
options.evidence_note: All ratings are untested illustrative estimates

options.name: Progressive configuration
options.description: Essential inputs first; advanced settings remain accessible and reversible
options.evidence_note: All ratings are untested illustrative estimates

options.name: Auto-detect and guided setup
options.description: Try detecting settings and guide the user through recovery when needed
options.evidence_note: All ratings are untested illustrative estimates

assessment.confidence_rationale: The design is consistent with published principles, but no direct task study or analytics are provided
assessment.risk_rationale: A design draft/prototype is reversible, but a poor setup experience could block task success. Production rollout would need its own risk review.

validation.method: Usability prototype comparison plus repository task coverage audit
validation.primary_metric: Successful first preview within task session
validation.invalidating_result: If users needing non-default configuration cannot discover it or recover from auto-detection errors, revise or choose another option
